commitResults.messageTitle: Add person needed to be modified to add students
commitResults.messageBody:
Since TutorEasy has tutors as its target audience, the person class was
modified to include the attributes of a student. The attributes added
are subjects, cost and lesson. The subjects attribute is a set of
subjects that the student is taking, the cost attribute is the cost of
the lesson and the lesson attribute is the day and time of the lesson.
The add command was also modified to include these attributes when
adding a new student. The edit command was also modified to include
 these attributes when editing a student. The person card was also
 modified to display these attributes when viewing a student.

commitResults.messageBody:

cases to the PersonTest.java file. These tests include checking the
toString method and ensuring that all attributes of the Person class
are correctly represented in the string output.

Keep subject parsing separate and delegate other find modes to the
existing parser to minimize overlap with the pending find changes.

Add parser, predicate, and integration tests and document the syntax.

Verify tests and style checks on upstream master and a temporary
combination with the fetched heads of PRs #59, #62, and #64. The
combined source merges without conflicts and passes the same checks.

To allow people to search for persons by their subjects, I have added a
new command called "subjectsearch" which allows users to search for
persons based on the subjects they are associated with. This feature
enhances the functionality of the application by providing a more
targeted search option.

Integrate the merged class-management and documentation changes while
preserving subject search and its tests.

The merge applies without conflicts. Verify the combined branch with
the full test suite and main and test style checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support batch enrolment in existing classes
commitResults.messageBody:
Class enrolment accepts only one student and requires a cost, even when
the class already exists. Enrolling a group therefore requires repeated
commands and repeated cost input.

Allow one or more displayed student indexes when enrolling in an
existing class. Reuse the recorded cost, skip students who are already
enrolled, and enrol the remaining students as unpaid.

Report both enrolled and skipped students. If every selected student is
already enrolled, leave the model unchanged and report that no changes
were made.

Update the user and developer guides and cover the new behavior with
parser and integration tests.

The tag command can add multiple tags to only one student at a time.
Assigning the same tag to a group therefore requires repeated commands.

Accept one or more displayed student indexes before a single t/TAG
argument. Validate all indexes and the tag before updating the model,
then add the tag to eligible students while reporting those already
tagged or at the tag limit.

Preserve the existing single-student syntax and document and test both
command forms.

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve order when processing batch enrolment
commitResults.messageBody:
Batch enrolment copied existing lessons into a HashSet, which could
reorder lessons during serialization. Duplicate index detection also
rescanned previously parsed indexes.

Use LinkedHashSet to preserve lesson order and track parsed indexes in
linear time. Add a regression test for lesson ordering.

Batch tagging updated each student separately and duplicated index
parsing logic. Its tests also did not verify non-display index order.

Prepare replacements before applying one atomic model update, reuse
ParserUtil for index parsing, centralize batch feedback, and add
regression tests for ordering and model notifications.
